subject.title: [Google Antigravity Ban] Frequent Tool Schema Reloading Causes False Positive Anti-Abuse Detection

question: Should OpenClaw land a bounded provider-normalized tool schema cache now, or defer this issue to the broader prepared-runtime migration?
rationale: The repeated work is visible in source, but the permanent cache boundary affects provider hooks, custom provider behavior, plugin metadata lifecycle, and the prepared-runtime roadmap.

options.title: Refresh bounded cache
options.body: Refresh or replace the open cache PR so known bundled normalizers can reuse cloned schema parameters while executable tool state stays per-turn.

options.title: Defer to prepared runtime
options.body: Keep this issue open until the prepared-runtime migration carries enough provider/tool facts to remove repeated normalization without a separate cache layer.

options.title: Require live provider proof
options.body: Hold implementation until current-main Google/Gemini live proof or heap evidence confirms the user-visible impact still happens.

recommendation.title: Refresh bounded cache
recommendation.body: Refresh or replace the open cache PR so known bundled normalizers can reuse cloned schema parameters while executable tool state stays per-turn.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision intersects the prepared-runtime migration tracker and provider/runtime boundary they already own in the related planning issue.
